parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text:
A lepton is an example of a fundamental particle.
State what is meant by fundamental particle.
parts.question_text_latex:

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
A lambda particle Λ^{0} is a hadron that consists of an up (u) quark, a down (d) quark and a
strange (s) quark.
Show that the charge on the Λ^{0} particle is zero.
parts.question_text_latex:
A lambda particle $Λ^{0}$ is a hadron that consists of an up (u) quark, a down (d) quark and a
strange (s) quark.
Show that the charge on the $Λ^{0}$ particle is zero.

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
The Λ^{0} particle is unstable. It can decay into a neutron (n) and a pion (π ^{0}) as shown by
Λ^{0}
n + π ^{0}.
The π ^{0} particle consists of an up quark and an up antiquark.
parts.question_text_latex:
The $Λ^{0}$ particle is unstable. It can decay into a neutron (n) and a pion ($\pi ^{0}$) as shown by
$Λ^{0}$
n + $\pi ^{0}$.
The $\pi ^{0}$ particle consists of an up quark and an up antiquark.
